HomeEssentials Inc. - Q2 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Inc. Q2 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Inc.'s results for the second quarter of fiscal 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Merchandising Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Stores Officer; and Casey Wong, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Alex.

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Inc.'s performance for the second quarter of fiscal 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Let me walk you through the highlights of our performance, starting with our overall results. As a leading brick-and-mortar player in the home essentials and lifestyle segment—blending elements of Home Depot's DIY focus with Williams-Sonoma's curated home goods—we're pleased to report resilient performance amid a choppy retail macro. Our comparable store sales growth, or comps, came in at +4.2% year-over-year for the quarter ended June 30th. This marks our fifth consecutive quarter of positive comps, exceeding our guidance range and Wall Street consensus. On a two-year stacked basis, that's a robust +7.2%, showing sustained momentum post-pandemic.

Unpacking the levers, foot traffic grew 1.8% year-over-year, powered by our Store Pulse initiative—an AI-driven in-store analytics tool that optimizes layouts and staffing during peaks, lifting conversion rates by 120 basis points to 28.5%. This shines in our mid-sized stores under 50,000 square feet, with 15% higher dwell times. Average ticket climbed 2.5% to $68.40, thanks to pricing discipline and more private label SKUs at 32% of sales, up from 28% last year. Average unit retail edged up 1.8%, highlighted by our Evergreen Essentials sustainable kitchen line appealing to millennials and Gen Z.

By merchandise category, hardlines and DIY at 45% of sales led with +5.6% comps—paint, tools, and outdoor living up 8.2% on easing raw material inflation and warm weather. Home décor and softlines at 35% grew 2.1%, bedding and rugs +4.3% via loyalty tweaks, though furniture softened to +0.8% on interest rate pressures. Apparel and accessories at 15% were flat amid weather issues, offset by private label athleisure +3.5%. Seasonal consumables at 5% exploded +12.4% on back-to-school prep.

Regionally, Southeast stores at 28% of base delivered +6.2% comps from hurricane recovery and BOPIS at 22% of sales. Midwest at 25% hit +4.1% on blue-collar tool demand, Northeast +3.5% post urban remodels, West Coast -0.5% from wildfires but e-comm pickups +7%, and Southwest +2.9% on expansion halo. Omnichannel helped, with store-fulfilled digital up 28% to 18% of comps sales, Scan & Go cutting shrinkage, inventory turns at 5.8.

These comps affirm our Brick-First, Digital-Enhanced strategy. We've sped remodels to 120 stores with RFID reducing stockouts 40%, and our HomeEssentials Rewards grew to 42 million members up 14%, shopping 3.2x more often and 22% higher per trip. We're gaining on Kohl's and Gap, matching TJX through value plays. For Q3, we see +3% to +5% comps with holiday partnerships like Yeti, agile pricing, and easing inflation tailwinds.

Next, e-commerce growth was a standout. E-commerce sales surged 28% year-over-year to $452 million—our best since pandemic peaks—beating industry 12-15% per NRF. Total sales hit $2.5 billion up 9%, digital now 18.1% mix from 14.2%. Mobile drove 65% of GMV with 42% traffic growth, AOV $145 on bundles in kitchen and outdoor up 35%. Conversions rose to 4.2% via AI recommendations on Adobe and SAP, cutting abandonment 22%.

Omnichannel shines: BOPIS 32% of orders lifted store traffic 15%, same-store sales 4.2%; ship-from-store at 85% of 1,200 locations cuts delivery to same/next-day for 70% urban areas, costs down 18%. AR app launch boosted millennial/Gen Z engagement 50%, downloads to 1.2 million. U.S. +32% to $380 million on home improvement; Europe +18% to $55 million post-HausGoods acquisition, softer Germany; Canada/Mexico +12%. Ahead, 22-27% growth with $150 million digital capex, DoorDash partnerships, CAC down 14% to $28, LTV $620. Gross margins 55% on digital aid investments. Vigilant on supply volatility and Temu.

Turning to store performance, let's break down traffic versus ticket in our Q2 comps. Comps at +4.2% is the gold standard for brick-and-mortar health, from stores open 12+ months including BOPIS at 18% fulfillment. This beat Q1's +2.8% and Johnson Redbook's -1.1% index, despite inflation and consumer confidence at 68.7.

Balanced drivers: traffic +1.8%, AOV +2.3%—60/40 ticket-heavy per our playbook favoring value over volume. Traffic via Placer.ai and counters at 1,200 doors improved from Q1 flat via Store Momentum 2.0: loyalty app geo-fencing +12% repeats from 62% members transacting 2.3x non-members; pop-ups in 150 stores like Dyson/Levi's +3% traffic, 14% dwell; BOPIS +22% converting Gen Z 40% higher. Conversion steady 28.5% vs. Macy's 26%, upside from AI greeters in 300 Q3 stores.

AOV $48.72 up from $47.61: UPT 2.1 +0.4%, AUR $23.21 +1.9%. Home Essentials 35% sales +4.1% ticket on 28% private label $65 vs $52 national; apparel 45% +1.8% on denim +12% AUR; footwear +0.9% athletic deflation. Promo down to 22%, Shelfgram AI +$2.50 AOV, margins 32.4% +150 bps.

Regions: Sunbelt/Southeast 42% doors +6.5% on +3.2% traffic same-day BOPIS; Northeast/Midwest 35% +2.1% ticket +2.4% affluent; West +1.8% ticket offset traffic dip, small formats planned. Outlook mid-single H2 comps, +2-3% traffic from 50 remodels, RFID curbside +25%. Gaining vs Kohl's/Walmart, hedged 65% essentials.

Now, marketing initiatives, where digital effectiveness accelerated growth. Digital channels supercharged stores at 72% revenue, attributing 28% Q2 traffic, 35% sales. ROAS 7.2x up 42% YoY from 5.1x, beating Macy's 5.8x; CAC $18.50 down 22%, CLV $285 +15%.

Channels: Google Performance Max 8.5x 45% of $145M spend; Meta 6.8x private label AOV $92 BOPIS; TikTok/Pinterest 9.2x apparel new customers 18%. CTR 2.1% +150 bps first-party data from 42M Rewards. Store hub: 62% digital to in-store pickup via RetailOS.

Privacy-first post-iOS/cookies: 78% first-party. Northeast/Midwest 34% traffic geofencing 4.2x Proximity Pulse 12.5% conversion; Sunbelt 22% TikTok apparel +8%; UK/Germany 9.1x +55%, Asia pilots 4.9x reallocating. CDP Snowflake/Tealium +28% email opens, GTM SS +$12M revenue; RMN $18M 12x ROAS.

Flywheel: digital shoppers basket $118 +16%, upsells 45%, Rewards churn -37% spend 2.3x. FY24 digital $650M +25% targeting 8.5x ROAS GeoLift. CPM up Meta but zero-party AR +24%. $1.2B attributable revenue 85% physical.

Supply chain optimization ties to shrink impact on margins. Shrink at 1.85% sales up 25 bps YoY to $28M loss, theft 68% $19M, rest internal 15%, admin 12%, vendor 5%. 32 bps gross margin drag to 32.4% down 45 bps YoY, masking 10 bps core gain. Aligns NRF 1.62% average, higher electronics 2.3%, H&B 1.95%.

Northeast/West Coast 2.15% ORC 450 incidents +30%; Midwest/Southeast 1.45-1.55%; Canada 1.70%. Trend spiked post-reopen, seasonal Q2. Fortress Retail $45M YTD: Verkada AI cameras 60% stores -15% shrink; RFID 75% apparel/50% electronics -25% admin; SCO Watchguard -28% theft; training, RILA advocacy.

Comps +2.8% beat index despite, small formats -20% shrink. FY24 shrink 1.65-1.70% +15-20 bps margin FY margin +50-75 bps.

On loyalty program updates and key guidance assumptions. FY2025 comps 2.5-4%, adj EPS $3.75-4.05, op margin +50-75 bps to 6-6.5%. Macro: GDP 2.3-2.6%, consumer spend 2.8-3.2%, unemp 4.1-4.3%, savings 3.5%, no big tariffs.

Traffic 1.5-2.5% Store as Hub BOPIS 28%, conv 28.5%; ASP flat-+1% private 42%. GM 38.2-38.7% +20 bps: inflation 2-2.5%, freight -25%, RFID 85% shrink -18%, promo 22-24%. SG&A 32-32.3% wage 3.5%, capex $450-500M 60% stores Sunbelt.

Regions: SE 4-6%, Midwest flat-2%, int'l +1%. Private 150 SKUs +200 bps, omni 65% local -12% costs, sustain 70% packaging +8 NPS GenZ +15%. Upside Fed cuts, downside conf <95. Hedged cash $1.2B.

Finally, sustainability initiatives and outlook. Q3 sales $2.45-2.55B +4-7%, comps 3-5% traffic 2-4%; digital 28% +8-10%. FY24 comps 4-6%, sales $10.2-10.5B +5%. U.S. 4-6% Sunbelt, Midwest 2-4%, int'l 5%.

GM +50-75 bps Q3 38.5% FY 38.2%: vendor direct -15% freight, RFID markdowns 22%, owned 35% +45% margins. SG&A 27.5% Q3 AI scheduling -8% payroll. EBITDA $425-475M Q3 FY $1.75-1.85B +12%, EPS $2.45-2.65 Q3 $8.20-8.60 FY. FCF $1.2B, debt/EBITDA 1.8x, inventory 12.5 weeks 5.2 turns.

Store 2.0 AR/stylist 200 stores +15% conv, recycled packaging 100% Q2 GenZ, DoorDash 500 stores. Headwinds unemp >4.2%, cotton +8%; 55/45 mix insulates +3% traffic.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to provide more details on our financial results.

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for Q2.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.5 billion, a 9% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 32.4%, primarily driven by improved sourcing and promotional discipline, partly offset by elevated shrink pressures. Operating expenses were $800 million, representing 32% of revenue. Net income was $150 million, or $1.20 per share. We generated $300 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently healthy at 12.5 weeks of supply, down 10% year-over-year with turns at 5.2x.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Taylor Kim, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Morgan Patel to discuss store operations, and then Casey Wong to discuss marketing initiatives.

Taylor Kim, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we launched our Evergreen Essentials sustainable kitchen line, which has seen strong uptake with double-digit comps in hardlines and higher AUR from premium private labels. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches like wellness SKUs.

Morgan Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Taylor. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented Store Momentum 2.0 remodels and AI greeters, and are seeing positive results with traffic up sequentially and conversion gains.

Casey Wong, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Morgan. Our Proximity Pulse geofencing campaign has increased brand awareness by 25%, driving 34% of traffic in key markets through hyper-local digital funnels.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions will now be repeated. Our first question comes from Chris Anderson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Chris Anderson (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Chris. Inflation has pressured consumer wallets, as seen in the Conference Board index at 68.7, but our balanced traffic-ticket growth and 65% essential-adjacent SKUs have made us resilient. Private label penetration at 28-42% and dynamic pricing captured incremental AOV, helping comps beat the index by 500+ bps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Good question, Mike. For Q3, we're targeting comps growth of 3% to 5%, with traffic acceleration from remodels and BOPIS, assuming stable macro and no major weather disruptions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Lisa. We've optimized with vendor-direct for 40% SKUs cutting freight 15%, RFID at 85% by year-start reducing shrink 18%, and micro-fulfillment in Sunbelt hubs enabling same-day for high-growth areas. These have supported margin expansion despite Red Sea issues.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Patel (Barclays):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
David, our HomeEssentials Rewards with 42 million members drove 12% repeat visits, 2.3x transaction rates, and basket upsells, contributing to 62% of traffic and key comp levers like UPT and CLV growth to $285-620. Digital integration keeps churn low at 37% less for acquired members.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session. I'll now turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
